title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 113
paragraphs: Thus passing by the Paeonians, Doberes, and Paeoples, who live beyond Pangaeum toward the north, he went on westward until at last he came to the river Strymon and the city of Eion, of which Boges — the man I was speaking of a little earlier — was commander as long as he lived. The country about Mount Pangaeum is called Phyllis; it stretches westward as far as the river Angites, which flows into the Strymon, and southward as far as the Strymon itself. At this river the Magi offered sacrifices for good omens, slaughtering white horses.
